card.title: Friction and momentum — where Newton's laws earn marks

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Force changes momentum (F = dp/dt, or F = ma at constant mass). In an isolated system total momentum never changes — recoil, collisions and explosions are all bookkeeping of one conserved ledger. Friction opposes relative motion or its imminence: static friction self-adjusts up to a ceiling, kinetic friction stays roughly constant once sliding.

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: F = ma = dp/dt · J = F·Δt = Δp (impulse)  ·  static f ≤ μs·N, kinetic f = μk·N, μs > μk  ·  limiting f = μs·N  ·  equilibrium: ΣF = 0 and Στ = 0, τ = r × F

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Newton's laws hold in inertial frames only. Momentum conservation needs zero net EXTERNAL force — internal forces (collisions, friction between parts) cannot change the total. Static friction matches the applied push exactly until the limiting value; beyond it, motion starts and kinetic takes over.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Action–reaction pairs never act on the same body, so they never cancel in a free-body diagram. A gun recoils because the bullet's forward momentum must be balanced. Moment equilibrium (τ clockwise = τ anticlockwise) decides see-saws, beams and hinges alongside force balance.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: 5 kg block, μs = 0.4 on a horizontal plane: normal N = mg = 49 N, limiting friction = μs·N = 0.4 × 49 = 19.6 N. Any push below 19.6 N is matched silently by static friction; 19.6 N is the minimum to start motion (NEB 2023, 3 marks).

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Newton breaks at near-light speeds (relativity) and atomic scales (quantum), and in accelerating frames unless pseudo-forces are added. Friction 'laws' are empirical approximations: μ depends on surface pair and condition, and the area-independence holds only approximately.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: From F = dp/dt with constant m: F = m·dv/dt = ma. Integrate over impact time: ∫F·dt = Δ(mv) = impulse-momentum theorem — the same statement behind airbags (long Δt, small F). For recoil: 0 = m_bullet·v + M_gun·V → V = −(m/M)v, momentum conserved from rest.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Always draw the free-body diagram first; friction points opposite the impending (not actual) motion. 'Smooth' means f = 0 — strike friction out. μs > μk always; if a question gives one μ, check which regime applies before multiplying.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: NEB 2024 (3): state Newton's three laws with one example each. NEB 2023 (3): 5 kg block, μs = 0.4 — horizontal force to start it sliding. Friction-vs-applied-force graph and moment-equilibrium numericals repeat most years.
